observation.visible_scene: A tight, mostly static close-up of a wet, textured metal surface (embossed lettering and a circular logo on the left, dark granular dirt patches on the right). A translucent white ice/frost patch with a rough, granular diagonal edge runs from the top toward the lower-center, separating the smooth wet area on the left from the bare dark surface on the right. A thin film of meltwater coats the left side, producing shifting bright reflections.
visible_changes: The reflective highlights in the water film on the left change position and intensity from frame to frame, indicating gentle movement of the surface water (or a slight camera/lighting shift) rather than a fixed scene.
The white ice patch keeps essentially the same outline, size and internal texture across the whole excerpt; its diagonal boundary does not visibly advance or retreat in any clear direction.
The embossed markings on the left become alternately more or less defined as the overlying water sheen moves, but the underlying pattern stays in place.
The dark dirt patches on the right remain stationary and unchanged.
The overall composition, framing and object positions are stable; no object translates or deforms noticeably.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the ice is net growing or net melting over a longer time (the excerpt is too short to show a directional change).
What causes the subtle water movement (wind, drip, vibration, or camera handling) and whether the surface is freezing or thawing.
Events before t=0 and after t=2.67 s, since both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
uncertain_details: Cannot definitively separate a slight camera jitter from reflection changes in the water film.
The exact phase-change direction (freezing vs. melting) of the central patch is not supported by visible boundary motion within this segment.
Material identity of the surface (metal cover vs. stone) is inferred from appearance only.
